items.title: Lopsided GST flexibility: India needs to resolve a stark asymmetry in this tax regime
items.summary: In India, the state has granted itself wide leeway on GST implementation timelines, but offers taxpayers no respite. While income-tax officials have the discretion to pardon delays by taxpayers who cite good reasons, GST doesn’t. This needs fixing.

items.title: India's internet startups are an inflection point: public investors aren’t buying private valuations blindly
items.summary: Zepto has held off its public share offer. Earlier listings—think Eternal, Nykaa and Delhivery—were judged by their reach and growth, with private valuations setting offer prices. But market investors now want platforms to show paths to profitability.

items.title: India must move quickly on digital trade—its agreement with the UK could play catalyst
items.summary: The India-UK comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) sets out a roadmap for easier cross-border trade by leveraging digital technologies. This should push India to quickly get its act together on various fronts.

items.title: How market participants read RBI's order of priority has a bearing on how well monetary policy works
items.summary: The decision to hold India’s policy rate steady in the face of inflation risks felt like a foregone conclusion. Now that RBI watchers appear to have assumed a hierarchy of policy goals, India’s central bank must mull over the potential consequences.

items.title: Hairpin bend ahead: what India must watch out for as it prepares to make vehicles talk to each other
items.summary: India’s proposed rollout of vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) connectivity to prevent traffic collisions marks a tech-enabled shift in the country’s road safety policy. As with driving, though, a slight slip-up could extract a heavy price. Proceed with caution.

items.title: First the Strait of Hormuz, then Bab el-Mandeb: maritime security has begun to shape the world order
items.summary: Seaborne trade chokepoints being leveraged or weaponized don’t bode well. The era of efficiency-driven globalization is giving way to one in which resilience, redundancy and maritime security shape the global order. India must focus on naval power.

items.title: Expand the investment options of Indian households: it’s an idea whose time may finally have come
items.summary: While hard restrictions on retail investors investing money abroad have served the country well so far, it's time for a change. Let’s ease capital controls so that market forces can reward investors and reduce India’s macro instability on the external front.

items.title: Employment anxiety: India needs jobs that offer a decent living wage and social security
items.summary: The country's employment statistics show new jobs being created, but many were in agriculture—a reversal of the shift away from farms any emerging economy sees. Meanwhile, euphoria over India’s rapid economic growth has stoked aspirations.

items.title: Don’t get Gen Z wrong: as this age cohort’s influence grows, it’s vital to understand what makes them tick
items.summary: Recent youth protests have placed Gen Z in the national spotlight. While views of their attitudes differ among older age groups, we need a reading of this generation that’s both in-depth and statistically representative. Here’s what we know.

items.title: Disaster display: the Assam floods reveal India’s outdated apparatus of climate finance
items.summary: Climate risk varies by river basins, but governance and finance are sliced up by administrative boundaries. This mismatch is smaller than the one in how funds are devolved to states. For anticipatory funding, here’s how Indian policy must evolve.

items.title: Climate finance may have gone up but an important promise by rich countries remains unmet
items.summary: The global discourse mustn’t obscure the data on flows from developed to developing countries—they amounted to just $58.7 billion in 2024. That’s much below what was committed and must not get papered over by other measures of progress.

items.title: China's policy of rare-earth export restrictions has already whittled down its monopoly power
items.summary: China’s control of the world’s rare-earth supply chain was okay till it decided to weaponize it against its geo-economic rivals. Several of these minerals are no longer in Beijing’s clutch and some others look set to escape as other countries get into the act.

items.title: Children must not be deprived of real learning in the process of trying to make education fun
items.summary: Even a well-meaning push for less burdensome education would fail if students aren’t encouraged to make an effort. We’ve seen this in India. Children from disadvantaged homes have borne the brunt of a concept that hardened into dogma.

items.title: August MPC huddle: why the Reserve Bank of India must change its stance at the very least
items.summary: Data on India’s economy shows that its growth versus inflation trade-off has been shifting inexorably this fiscal year. The central bank’s Monetary Policy Committee should act fast—before it gets too late.

items.title: As EU-China trade friction grows, Beijing had better pay attention to Brussels’ concerns
items.summary: Beijing’s recent paper in defence of its trade practices is unlikely to soften Brussels. Instead of sticking to its guns, China should act to pre-empt European barriers. The People’s Republic must learn to empathize with trade partners reeling from a China shock.

items.title: Are open-weight AI models like Kimi available for anyone to use? Not quite. Here's why
items.summary: While open-weight models allow users to freely download their weights, that doesn’t grant us the compute power needed for high inference tasks at the AI frontier. Users in India will benefit only once we serve intelligence on our own infrastructure.

items.title: Anthropic versus Nvidia differ on how to contain Chinese AI—model barriers or chip denial?
items.summary: The two tech giants are at odds amid US confusion over the rise of Chinese AI. While one sees AI models as a point of intervention, the other supports chip export restrictions. Each has a self-interest at stake, but is that what should determine US policy?

items.title: AI movies aren't all slop—for some aspiring filmmakers they can be empowering
items.summary: Filmmaking is an art of storytelling that AI could surely help sharpen. It also opens this art form up to those with modest budgets. Just as human involvement doesn't guarantee artistry, AI assistance needn’t translate into soulless slop.
